headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill directs Virginia's primary electric provider to establish rates that recover costs for increasing electric generating capacity from customers with 25 MW or more in electric demand, effectively requiring data centers to pay for their own infrastructure.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Senator L. Louise Lucas, community advocates, Virginia Conservation Network.
opponents: Data centers, large energy users, Data Center Coalition.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to Users
news_summary: Virginia's legislature passed HB 1393, which requires the State Corporation Commission to establish rates that make large energy users, such as data centers, responsible for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity. This measure aims to prevent these costs from being passed on to other customers, particularly residential ratepayers.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This legislation requires proposed industrial facilities, including data centers, to submit annual water consumption estimates to allow for impact consideration during rezoning and special use permit decisions.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental advocates, community groups, Virginia Conservation Network.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Increases Data Center Water Reporting Requirements
news_summary: Senate Bill 553, now awaiting the governor's signature, aims to increase transparency by requiring data centers to report their water consumption. This measure provides communities with clearer insight into local resource use, addressing concerns about the industry's significant water demands.

headline: Establish Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring zoning applicants to conduct site assessments examining sound profiles on nearby homes and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Josh Thomas, community advocates, Virginia Conservation Network.
opponents: Data center developers, former Governor Glenn Youngkin.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Mandates Data Center Siting Impact Assessments
news_summary: HB 153, passed by the legislature, introduces a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and schools. It also grants localities the power to demand assessments on potential impacts to water, agriculture, and historic resources.
